results.scope: Hypergraphs are finite families of finite sets on an arbitrary vertex type; a Berge-C5 has an injective vertex map and an injective hyperedge map from Fin 5 with v i, v (i + 1) in e i, and no inducedness or linearity condition; saturation quantifies over every absent three-element set; satNumber n is the least size of a saturated hypergraph on Fin n, isolated vertices included.

Closing a four-edge Berge path by an absent set containing its ends gives a Berge-C5; a Berge-C5 uses five distinct hyperedges, so a saturated hypergraph on at least four vertices has at least four hyperedges.
Two rooted pieces on arbitrary finite vertex types glued at their roots form a rooted piece whose non-root orders and sizes add; a Berge-C5 cannot cross the cut vertex.

results.paper_label: prop:interval and thm:main (the range from ceil(2(n-1)/3) to n-2, and n-1 when 4 divides n-1)
results.scope: For every n >= 14 and every m with 2(n - 1) <= 3m and m <= n - 2 a saturated hypergraph on Fin n with m hyperedges; for every n >= 7 one with 2n/3 = ceil(2(n - 1)/3) hyperedges (natural-number division), hence satNumber n <= 2n/3; and one with n - 1 hyperedges when n >= 5 and 4 divides n - 1. The pieces are glued at the root; the families B(p,q,t) with unbounded parameters are not formalized.
